acceptance: Record real upstream identity, fork protected integration and complete fork validation/delivery provenance at the actual merged source SHA.
Record core adoption PR, trusted delivery origin/hash binding, minimal core integration/packaging proof, ordinary review/CI and protected squash merge.
Live core develop pin/archive identity is the accepted delivery or a subsequently newer accepted delivery; no routine manual producer or consumer command was needed.
No eligible clean release means certification remains open with the external wait explicit, never a manufactured no-op success.
context:
Owner instruction 2026-11-05 supersedes BOTH rejected designs. benchbox-sqlglot owns upstream discovery/integration, fork PR lifecycle, source/relocation/runtime/engine/distribution validation and trustworthy wheel delivery. BenchBox core owns consuming that delivery, origin/identity/hash binding, transactional pin updates, its own wrapper/benchmark-definition/installed-package concerns and ordinary core PR landing. Core must not discover upstream, merge fork PRs, reconstruct/re-review fork source, repeat fork test matrices or acquire a fork-write credential. Theseus stays unchanged and generic; no special policy, external-source inlet, synthetic dataset, second model-review path or reviewer release is needed. Theseus PR25 closed unmerged; prior approval claims withdrawn. This supersedes the source-review-at-core portion of sqlglot-fork-review-h1-governance, not existing protected-branch rules or ordinary review requirements. Preserve exact merged-SHA producer evidence, scoped independent credentials, no candidate execution with write/reviewer secrets, no golden/outcome/test/waiver changes, reviewed rollback, human holds/disarms, reverted-delivery suppression and no public release/cloud spend. Update current fork/core runbooks to this boundary. Corrected proposal: local://sqlglot-end-to-end-proposal.md. The live tracker, not discarded branch code or prior notes, owns delivery state.

v30.30.0 does NOT certify: the chain ran end to end (fork #85 merged by controller, delivery run 42326062924, core #3997 opened/armed/merged by the App), but it needed manual dispatches (fork controller x2, core consumer x2) and one failed-job CI rerun for the known sqlite q16 timeout, so "no routine manual producer or consumer command" is not met. Certification waits on the next upstream SQLGlot release flowing on the schedules alone (fork 05:41 UTC, core 06:37 UTC) after activation finishes.

Activation is now done and no longer an unmet dependency. Certification remains open waiting for the next real upstream release through schedule/event automation without manual producer/consumer commands. Fork event/readiness changes landed#86; core event/readiness batch remains blocked on normal host verification admission, with owner freeing memory. Do not certify the manually advanced30.30.0 chain.

2026-11-12: upstream v30.31.0 does not count toward certification. The fork refresh stopped on a carried-patch conflict (benchbox-sqlglot issue #88) and was refreshed by hand (benchbox-sqlglot #89); core adoption #4128 was opened by hand after four delivery dispatches hit startup_failure during the 2026-11-11 GitHub Actions incident. A dry-run dispatch on 2026-11-12 (run 43237227759) passed readiness with state current. Certification still needs the next upstream release end to end without manual steps. Risk reducers filed on the fork tracker: carried-patch-drift-unseen-until-release-20261112, controller-conflict-outcome-reports-success-20261112, not-offered-patches-lack-upstream-follow-up-20261112.

2026-11-17: upstream v30.32.0 (tagged 2026-11-16) and v30.33.0 (tagged 2026-11-17) will not certify. Five carried patches conflict with v30.33.0, so the fork refresh needs manual adaptation (benchbox-sqlglot tracker: refresh-upstream-v30-33-0-patch-conflicts-20261117). Certification needs a later upstream release that the fork refreshes and core adopts with no manual steps. Also unobserved so far: a delivery arm triggered by workflow_run on a real chore/sqlglot-* adoption PR since the branch filter landed in #4233 (merged 2026-11-14 as 1a9b75f9); the certifying release must show that path (or the scheduled recheck) arming the adoption PR. Schedule timing risk: sqlglot-delivery-schedules-start-hours-late-20261117.

2026-11-17: 30.33.0.1 adoption (PR #4289) needed a person to record a golden-corpus change (upstream d78ad66c BigQuery INFORMATION_SCHEMA quoting), on top of the manual fork refresh, so it does not certify. Positive evidence: the delivery App opened #4289 itself and a delivery run fired from workflow_run on the chore/sqlglot-30.33.0.1 branch after the #4233 filter. A certifying release must also change no recorded corpus output unless sqlglot-adoption-blocked-by-golden-corpus-change-20261117 changes that.

Owner decision 2026-11-17 (choice dialog): a release certifies when no person acts between the upstream tag and core's merge of the adoption. Patches staged before the tag (fork stage-drift-resolutions-before-upstream-tags-20261117) are routine maintenance and do not disqualify it. A corpus change re-recorded by the delivery automation (sqlglot-adoption-blocked-by-golden-corpus-change-20261117) does not disqualify it either.

2026-11-25: upstream v30.35.0 does not qualify. BenchBox's scheduled sqlglot-delivery job refused fork 30.35.0.1 (retirement check: sqlite-month-interval now passes with 2024-02-29), and the owner chose a person-made adoption of 30.35.0.2 with a fork SQLite guard (sqlglot-adopt-30-35-0-2). This item waits for the next upstream release that flows through untouched.
description: After capability activation, observe one real eligible clean upstream release through FORK-owned discovery/refresh/protected merge, complete fork validation and trusted exact-merged-SHA wheel delivery, then CORE-only download/identity/hash binding, transactional pin update, unique consumer integration/packaging checks, ordinary core review/CI and protected squash merge. No core source reconstruction or second semantics review, no Theseus changes, no routine manual merge/build/adopt command. Record actual version/SHAs/run/attempt/artifact/digest, fork PR and core adoption PR identities plus live develop pin/archive hash. A no-op or exception-only release does not prove success. If none is eligible, remain open rather than fabricate a tag or production pin-change probe.
